title: When connecting to openconnect VPN focus is not automatically on the input fields
line: In the OpenConnect VPN login dialog you can type your username, password and MFA code right away, without clicking into each field first.
explanation: The OpenConnect auth widget called setFocus() on its PasswordField, which is a plain container widget around the real line edit, so the focus landed on the container and typing went nowhere. It also did this while building the form, before the form's layout was added to the dialog's login box; that reparenting clears the focus again. PasswordField now forwards focus to its line edit with setFocusProxy(), and the OpenConnect form remembers its first empty field and focuses it once the form is in the dialog.

commits.message:
openconnect: put the keyboard focus in the login form's first empty field

PasswordField is a container around a line edit, so setFocus() on it left
the focus on the container, and the form was focused before being added to
the dialog, which drops the focus. Add a focus proxy and focus it later.

BUG: 506021

media.caption: Master: typed 'alice', 'secret' and '123456' right after each form appeared; all three fields stay empty
Fixed: the same typing lands in the Username, Password and MFA code fields
Master: the whole dialog after typing 'alice' into the username form
Fixed: the whole dialog after typing 'alice' into the username form

review.text: Accurately identifies and fixes both root causes of the missing keyboard focus in the OpenConnect auth dialog: adding setFocusProxy(m_passwordField) to PasswordField fixes focus forwarding across plasma-nm, and deferring setFocus() until after d->ui.loginBoxLayout->addLayout(layout) prevents reparenting from clearing focus. End-to-end verification across username, password, and MFA forms plus Tab-order regression checks on other dialogs are thorough.
